Intervals and TreeSHAP make estimates auditable
Railway delay prediction and platform scheduling
A symmetric residual interval is calibrated on held-out calibration dates. For each uploaded prediction, TreeSHAP shows which inputs raise or lower the estimate relative to the model baseline.
Positive contribution: pushes predicted delay higher.
Negative contribution: pushes predicted delay lower.
SHAP is an explanation of the fitted model, not causal evidence.

TreeSHAP uses XGBoost native pred_contribs on the fitted pipeline. Five-row NDLS check maximum additive reconstruction error was 0.000042 min. Literature: Lundberg & Lee (2017), NeurIPS 30; Gao et al. (2024).

Two hard constraints are checked in every schedule
Railway delay prediction and platform scheduling
Each platform is a single-capacity resource. An overlength train is left unassigned. A service cannot start until the prior simulated dwell and clearance have ended.
Default demo: six 700 m platforms; configurable from 4–8 platforms.
Configured scenario inputs are synthetic because verified station infrastructure is not available in the project extract.
Zero modeled violations do not certify real signal, route, braking or interlocking safety.
These are simplified software checks, not an operational railway safety case.
SimPy models platform occupancy as limited resources
Railway delay prediction and platform scheduling

FCFS assigns each movement to the compatible platform available earliest. Both policies use the same arrival stream, lengths, dwell and clearance. The simulator reports wait, utilization, throughput and service count.
SimPy is a process-based discrete-event simulation framework with limited-capacity shared resources: https://simpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/simpy_intro/shared_resources.html
The busy case reaches FCFS after a wait safeguard

Railway delay prediction and platform scheduling
The fast replay uses single-capacity platform queues and tracks static conflicts before queue recovery separately from resource collisions after recovery.
Randomized ranges are explicit scenario assumptions, not empirical railway failure distributions.
Default case has low wait; conflict risk appears in 10.2% of runs
Railway delay prediction and platform scheduling
1,021 / 10,000 runs had a static conflict risk; 0 queue-resource collisions after recovery.

10,000 runs, seed 2068. Static conflict risk means nominal platform reservations overlap after perturbation. Zero post-queue resource collisions are guaranteed by the exclusive resource model and are not a safety certification.
